subject: Follow-up: target unit economics & host parity
messages:
From: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
To: Sabrina Liu <sabrina@finlytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 9 Jun 2027 15:14:00 +0000
Subject: Follow-up: target unit economics & host parity
Attachments: redwood-price-worksheet.csv

Sabrina — great to meet earlier. Quick recap and the asks we discussed so we can align on next steps.

Recap from today's discovery
- Current traffic profile: ~25M tokens/month steady; spikes to ~100M tokens in marketing-driven bursts.
- Primary workloads: customer support summaries, 1–3-shot retrieval-augmented generation for account pages.
- SLA needs: 95th p95 latency target ~350ms and regional redundancy in us-east.

Pricing & unit-econ conversation notes
- You said target effective cost goal is in the low tens per 1M tokens (ballpark).
- Procurement asked for competitive comparisons vs OpenAI/Anthropic and any quantized-hosted options.

Our take (ballpark) — for alignment only
- OpenAI (current/generative endpoints): ~$20–$30 per 1M tokens depending on model & chat vs single-turn pricing.
- Anthropic (baseline chat variants): ~$22–$28 per 1M for standard tiers.
- Open-model hosts (quantized / 8-bit): can be materially cheaper ($8–$15 per 1M) but often trade-offs on latency and occasional output quality.

What I'd like from you
1) Confirm the monthly committed volume range you expect to sign to (options you mentioned: 25M steady / 50–75M expected in Q3 / 100M peak).
2) Confirm target $/1M token range that would make Redwood an easy choice for procurement (e.g., $X–$Y per 1M).
3) Procurement timeline and whether you need an estimated SOW / draft commercial terms before we do a formal pricing call.

Next steps (ours)
- I'll share a short price worksheet (attached) with three tiered offers: no-commit, small commit (monthly), and a 12‑month reserved tier with stepped unit rates and burst allowances.
- Marissa will run a quick host-parity sketch vs OpenAI/Anthropic/open-host assumptions and include impact on monthly bill and latency risk.
- If the worksheet looks reasonable we can schedule a procurement call next week and share SOC2 + encryption docs.

Thanks again — I think there's a clear path to align commercially if we can get the commit/budget band.

Connor

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Sabrina Liu <sabrina@finlytics.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 09:30:00 +0000
Subject: RE: Follow-up: target unit economics & host parity

Sabrina / Connor — looping in a quick competitive pass from a pricing & unit-econ perspective. Attaching redwood-soc2-summary.pdf.

High-level pricing sketches (illustrative, final to be framed into a commercial term sheet):
- No-commit (pay-as-you-go): $18 per 1M tokens — good for short pilots, higher unit cost.
- Monthly commit (12-month minimum; mid-tier): $12 per 1M tokens for 50M+ committed/mo equivalent.
- Reserved (annual/volume-backed) tier: $8 per 1M tokens for 100M+ effective committed throughput.

Competitive parity (what to expect in the market):
- OpenAI / managed chat tier: typically $20–$30 per 1M for feature-complete endpoints; discounts for committed spend.
- Anthropic: similar band to OpenAI depending on model family.
- Self-hosted/open-host (quantized): can be as low as $6–$12 per 1M but you incur ops/latency risk and less predictable quality.

Quick unit-econ worked example using your steady-state (25M tokens/mo) and Q3 ramp to 75M:
- Scenario A (no-commit): 25M * ($18/1M) = $450/mo; ramp to 75M = $1,350/mo.
- Scenario B (monthly commit ~50M equivalent @ $12/1M): 25M -> $300/mo; 75M -> $900/mo.
- Scenario C (reserved 100M tier @ $8/1M): 25M -> $200/mo; 75M -> $600/mo.

Notes: these are illustrative — final numbers will depend on exact model mix (chat vs single-turn), embedding volumes, and any additional features (streaming, function-calls). Latency SLOs and regional routing may affect available discounts.

Proposed next steps (to hit procurement timeline)
1) Connor — can you send the price worksheet updated to two commercial options: (A) 12-month monthly-commit at $12/1M and (B) 12-month reserved ladder to $8/1M for 100M+ effective throughput.
2) I'll prepare a short commercial summary (one-pager) that maps those options to expected monthly bill at 25/50/75/100M.
3) We will include the SOC2 summary + encryption and data retention bullets for procurement.

If procurement wants a signed LOI to hold pricing while legal redlines, we can explore that — Connor, flag the team if we should prepare a short LOI template.

Marissa Cole
Sales Lead, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
